subject.title: RFC: Skill routing metadata and evaluation hints for Harness-style OpenClaw setups

question: Should ClawHub establish optional routing and verification metadata as a general public registry contract, and which advisory fields are safe and useful enough for a minimal v1?
rationale: The request changes public skill/plugin manifests and API semantics, while field selection, consumer neutrality, anti-gaming policy, and the boundary between author claims and trusted security state require maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve a narrow advisory v1
options.body: Define normalized intents plus human-readable verification hints, expose raw metadata through API and CLI, and defer ranking and author-declared risk levels until evaluated against real consumers.

options.title: Require consumer validation first
options.body: Keep the RFC open but require the linked Harness work to provide a prototype, task corpus, and routing-quality results before freezing any ClawHub fields.

options.title: Decline registry routing metadata
options.body: Keep ClawHub focused on discovery and package facts, leaving routing, risk classification, and completion checks entirely to external control layers.

recommendation.title: Approve a narrow advisory v1
recommendation.body: Define normalized intents plus human-readable verification hints, expose raw metadata through API and CLI, and defer ranking and author-declared risk levels until evaluated against real consumers.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged work introduced the current parsed skill metadata surface most directly affected by this contract decision.
